new_entities.name: Oral dutasteride in men
aliases: dutasteride for male pattern hair loss
new_entities.description: Oral dutasteride therapy used in male androgenetic alopecia.

edges.effect_quant: In a 917-man randomized trial, dutasteride 0.5 mg/day improved hair count and width more than placebo and also outperformed finasteride 1 mg/day at 24 weeks. Later network meta-analyses consistently rank dutasteride at or near the top of non-surgical monotherapies for male AGA.
edges.population: adult men with androgenetic alopecia treated with oral dutasteride monotherapy
edges.mechanism: Dutasteride inhibits both type I and type II 5-alpha reductase, suppressing scalp dihydrotestosterone more strongly than finasteride and thereby slowing follicular miniaturization.
edges.summary: Oral dutasteride is one of the strongest pharmacologic hair-regrowth signals in the male AGA literature. The direct trial and network-level evidence both point to meaningful efficacy, although the tradeoff profile is also why it remains more debated than standard topical minoxidil.
edges.caveats: This payload covers efficacy, not sexual or fertility concerns, which belong on separate harms edges. Stronger efficacy does not automatically mean better real-world acceptability for every patient.

evidence.citation: OlsenEA et al 2014 J Am Acad Dermatol
evidence.notes: A randomized, active- and placebo-controlled study of the efficacy and safety of different doses of dutasteride versus placebo and finasteride in the treatment of male subjects with androgenetic alopecia.
Relative Efficacy of Minoxidil and the 5-α Reductase Inhibitors in Androgenetic Alopecia Treatment of Male Patients: A Network Meta-analysis.

evidence.citation: GuA et al 2025 J Cosmet Dermatol
evidence.notes: Relative Efficacy of Conventional Monotherapies and Select Nonconventional, Over-the-Counter Products for Male Androgenetic Alopecia: A Network Meta-Analysis Study.
